findings.description: Multi-writer persistence defects recurred. R5 F-1 (critical): write marker was a per-page counter, two writers collided, reconcile claimed 'synced' and the next save erased the other writer's events. R5 left R3-F2 (non-atomic cross-tab localStorage read-merge-write) as a known limit; fixture mode short-circuits the store (PersistencePort.fs:212) so specs never exercised it. In R6 it became R6-D-002 (critical, open): without navigator.locks one or two tabs' changes lost every run; two fallback designs failed. R6-D-001: restore showed 'Saved to GitHub (confirmed …)' for other writers' device-only changes. Arca reconciliation also lacks byte read-back (pre-fix F-1 shape).
findings.rootCause: Local persistence used two non-atomic storage calls with no lock or storage-event merge; confirmation by ancestry/marker instead of read-back.
findings.preventableByConvention: Single-owner or locked cross-tab persistence with explicit no-locks fallback; deterministic split-step race test in Chromium and WebKit; fixture mode must use the real store.

findings.description: F# structure inconsistencies: two JSON codecs (src/engine/Json.fs and src/persistence/Json.fs) with no recorded reuse justification; stepOr silently swallows book faults (persistence/Sync.fs:199-202); a book that fails to decode silently falls back to Book.initial, downgrading a stored Unknown to Disconnected; ReadBack trusts a caller-computed bool.

findings.preventableByConvention: One serialization module per contract; Result-based error model with no silent fallbacks.
